lessons.subject: Mathematics
lessons.title: Solving linear equations
lessons.overview: An equation is balanced: whatever you do to one side must also be done to the other. Work backwards through the operations around the unknown.
keyPoints: Simplify each side first.
Undo addition or subtraction before multiplication or division.
Substitute your answer into the original equation to check it.

example.question: Solve 3x + 5 = 20.
steps: Subtract 5 from both sides: 3x = 15.
Divide both sides by 3: x = 5.

lessons.subject: Physics
lessons.title: Speed, distance and time
lessons.overview: Speed measures how quickly distance changes. Keep units consistent before using the relationship speed = distance ÷ time.
keyPoints: Speed = distance ÷ time.
Distance = speed × time.
Average speed uses total distance and total time.

example.question: A cyclist covers 600 m in 40 s. Find the average speed.
steps: Identify distance = 600 m and time = 40 s.
Divide distance by time: 600 ÷ 40.
State the unit in metres per second.

lessons.subject: Chemistry
lessons.title: Inside the atom
lessons.overview: Atoms contain protons and neutrons in a nucleus, with electrons arranged around it. Their numbers explain charge, mass and identity.
keyPoints: Atomic number equals the number of protons.
Mass number equals protons plus neutrons.
A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.

example.question: An atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. Find its particles.
steps: Protons = atomic number = 11.
Electrons = protons for a neutral atom = 11.
Neutrons = 23 − 11.

lessons.subject: Biology
lessons.title: Cell structures and functions
lessons.overview: Cells are the basic units of life. Their specialised structures carry out jobs such as controlling activity, releasing energy and making proteins.
keyPoints: The nucleus contains genetic material and controls the cell.
Mitochondria release energy through respiration.
Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole.

example.question: Why do muscle cells contain many mitochondria?
steps: Muscle contraction needs energy.
Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration releases energy.
More mitochondria support the cell's high energy demand.
example.answer: They release the energy needed for repeated contraction.

lessons.subject: English
lessons.title: Subject–verb agreement
lessons.overview: A verb must agree with its subject in number and person. Identify the true subject before choosing the verb form.
keyPoints: A singular subject normally takes a singular verb.
Words between subject and verb do not change the agreement.
After does or doesn't, use the base form of the main verb.

example.question: Choose: The box of books is/are heavy.
steps: The complete subject is 'the box of books'.
The head noun is the singular word 'box'.
Choose the singular verb 'is'.
example.answer: The box of books is heavy.

lessons.subject: Economics
lessons.title: How price affects demand
lessons.overview: Demand describes how much consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices. Price changes cause movement along a demand curve.
keyPoints: For a normal good, a higher price usually lowers quantity demanded.
A price change causes movement along the curve.
Income, tastes and related-goods prices can shift the whole curve.

example.question: The price of cinema tickets falls while other factors stay constant. What happens?
steps: Only the good's own price changed.
Apply the law of demand.
Show a movement along, rather than a shift of, the demand curve.

lessons.subject: Geography
lessons.title: Reading contour lines
lessons.overview: Contour lines connect points of equal height. Their pattern lets you interpret elevation, slope and landforms on a flat map.
keyPoints: Close contour lines show a steep slope.
Wide spacing shows a gentle slope.
The contour interval is the vertical difference between adjacent lines.

example.question: Contours rise from 100 m to 160 m in intervals of 20 m. How many height steps are there?
steps: Find the height change: 160 − 100 = 60 m.
Divide by the contour interval: 60 ÷ 20.

lessons.subject: Government
lessons.title: Purpose of a constitution
lessons.overview: A constitution sets the fundamental rules of government. It defines institutions, distributes power and protects agreed rights.
keyPoints: It states the powers and limits of government.
It explains relationships among government institutions.
It may be written or unwritten, rigid or flexible.

example.question: Why can separation of powers protect citizens?
steps: Power is distributed among institutions.
Each institution can restrain abuses by the others.
This reduces the chance that one body controls every state function.
example.answer: It limits concentrated power through institutional checks.

lessons.subject: Literature
lessons.title: Simile and metaphor
lessons.overview: Figurative comparisons create meaning beyond literal description. A simile signals its comparison; a metaphor states one thing as another.
keyPoints: A simile commonly uses 'like' or 'as'.
A metaphor makes a direct comparison.
Explain the effect of the comparison in its context.

example.question: What does 'Her voice was velvet' suggest?
steps: It directly identifies the voice as velvet, so it is a metaphor.
Velvet feels smooth and soft.
Transfer those qualities to the sound of the voice.
example.answer: The metaphor suggests a soft, smooth and pleasant voice.

lessons.subject: Computer Science
lessons.title: Thinking in algorithms
lessons.overview: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of unambiguous steps for solving a problem. Good algorithms are correct, clear and efficient.
keyPoints: Sequence runs instructions in order.
Selection chooses a path based on a condition.
Iteration repeats instructions while or until a condition is met.

example.question: Describe an algorithm that finds the largest number in a list.
steps: Store the first item as the current largest.
Compare each remaining item with it.
Replace the stored value whenever a larger item is found.
example.answer: After the final comparison, the stored value is the largest.
